title: Cost Ratios Change Who Gets Flagged: Operating Points for Wearable Stress Detection on Public Corpora
content: Wearable stress detectors are often summarized with a single accuracy or area under the curve. Those numbers do not say which probability cutoff was used, or how the balance between missed high-strain windows and false alerts changes when that cutoff moves. This paper recomputes operating characteristics from published subject-independent evaluation cells on WESAD (n = 694 windows; 155 stress-positive) and on a PhysioNet wearable stress and exercise release (n = 100 sessions). Two cost policies are compared: equal weighting of misses and false alerts, and a 5:1 weighting that treats misses as five times costlier. On WESAD, the 5:1 rule raises the flag rate from 0.215 to 0.301 and false positives from 44.7 to 96.5 per 1,000 windows. Avoiding 24 false negatives costs 36 additional false positives, or 1.50 extra false positives per miss avoided. Uncalibrated cross-corpus transfer closes 68% of the gap to perfect ranking in one direction and 20% in the other. We treat that arithmetic as a checkable account of how a one-line cost assumption reshapes the alert stream; nothing here recommends that an employer adopt these particular cutoffs.
